objective: Review the code changes of commit 386cb22 (range eee082a..386cb22) for correctness and regressions.
scope: packages/runtime/src/state/tree.ts (gitBounded detached spawn and killGroup, stageState), packages/runtime/src/setup/settings.ts and cli/setup.ts (450000, effort auto handling), cli/sessioncontext.ts, and their tests. Instruction-text and docs changes in the same commit are out of scope; they get rewritten next.

criteria.text: Process groups: a timed-out or interrupted state fetch kills its whole process group without killing the CLI itself or leaking zombies, on Linux and macOS
Staging: stageState stages tracked changes and force-adds only record and config paths, never a stray ignored file, and still commits new records in every state mode
Effort auto: doctor and setup no longer flag an Opus 5.5 modelSettings entry whose effortLevel /effort auto removed, and still recommend effort when no entry exists
Regressions: no existing behavior breaks; each fix has a test that fails without it

blockers:
- `packages/runtime/src/state/tree.ts` (`stageState`, `STATE_FILE`): the regex only admits `config.json` and `intents/*/{intent.json, assignments|branches|pulls/*.json}`. `holyagent migrate` copies legacy notes (`resume-notes.md`, `notes/**`) into the Intent folder (`legacy.ts` 533-551, `migrate.ts` `writeAll`) and then calls `commitState`. Those files are untracked and match neither `add -u` nor the regex, so they are not committed and stay loose in the state worktree. The old `add -f -A` committed them. This breaks the documented "notes copied unchanged" behavior for the state branch. `migrate.test.ts` passes anyway because it does not check that the notes are committed. Fix: also stage the migrated note paths (a `commitState` argument, or add the note folders to the staged set), and add a test that asserts they are in `git ls-tree` of the state branch.

questions: none

notes:
- Optional: `detached: true` puts git in its own session, so a terminal Ctrl-C (or a kill of the CLI) during a fetch leaves git and ssh running until they time out. The release handler only runs on Effect interruption, and `src` has no signal handler. Before this change Ctrl-C reached git too. The timeout and Effect-interrupt paths do kill the group, and the awaited `child.exited` leaves no zombie of git itself.
- Optional: `stageState` passes every record path to `git add` as argv and globs the whole `.holyagent` tree on each commit. Large states could hit the Windows command-line limit; Linux has about 2 MB of room. Batching or using `git status --porcelain` would avoid it.
- Optional: `defaultsFor` treats any Opus 5.5 entry without `effortLevel`, including `{}` or `{autoCompactWindow}`, as "cleared by `/effort auto`". That is the accepted ambiguity, and a fresh settings file still gets the recommendation (covered by the fresh-machine test).

evidence:
Process groups: `tree.ts` `gitBounded` uses `detached: true` plus `process.kill(-pid, SIGKILL)` on timeout and on a Failure/interrupt exit, and ignores a group that is already gone. The test "a fetch killed at its timeout leaves no helper process running" passes on the snapshot and fails on eee082a. Linux only; macOS not run (macOS relies on Bun's setsid for `detached`).
Staging: the test "a stray file that its own ignore rule covers is never committed, a record always is" passes and fails on eee082a. It covers the ignored base `.gitignore` case. BLOCKED by the migrate-notes regression above: the notes copied by `migrate` are not committed.
Effort auto: the new doctor test passes and fails on eee082a, and the 450000 setup tests pass, so a cleared entry is not flagged. The fresh-machine setup test (passes) shows the level is still recommended when no entry exists.
Regressions: each fix has a failing-without-fix test (7 fail on the eee082a code), but the migrate-notes commit regression is untested and breaks existing behavior.
